newsitem.title: GERMANY: FDP deputy urges German Eurofighter delay.
newsitem.headline: FDP deputy urges German Eurofighter delay.

text.p: A leading deputy from Germany's Free Democrats (FDP), junior partners in Germany's ruling coalition, said on Monday that Bonn's budget woes meant a decision on buying the Eurofighter combat aircraft should be postponed.

"The financing of the procurement is completely unrealistic and cannot be borne by the state budget," FDP deputy Juergen Koppelin, a member of parliament's budget committee responsible for defence, said.
A decision to go ahead and buy the Eurofighter would barely win support just as Finance Minister Theo Waigel is likely to slap a freeze on state spending, Koppelin added in a statement.
FDP headquarters, however, said Koppelin was expressing his personal opinion, and the party had not yet adopted a position over procuring Eurofighter.
A Defence Ministry spokesman also denied Koppelin's assertion that Eurofighter would be on the agenda for a meeting on Tuesday of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet.

Defence Minister Volker Ruehe has agreed a 23 billion mark ($14 billion) price tag for Eurofighter with Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), German partner in the four-country project. He has said he expects parliamentary approval in the first quarter.
Newspapers have reported that Waigel and Ruehe have also reached agreement in principle over splitting the initial extra costs of Germany's Eurofighter force between the defence and federal budgets.

But the money has not been factored into the 1997 budget, which aims to ensure that Germany will qualify for European monetary union in 1999 with a budget deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product. The Maastricht treaty sets a deficit limit of three percent of GDP.

A German decision to buy is eagerly awaited by the three other countries involved in developing the 21st-century combat jet. Also members of the Eurofighter consortium are British Aerospace, Italy's Alenia ALEI.RO and CASA of Spain.
